title: ChatGPT Generated Training Plans for Runners are not Rated Optimal by Coaching Experts, but Increase in Quality with Additional Input Information
authors: Düking P, Sperlich B, Voigt L, Van Hooren B, Zanini M, Zinner C
journal: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine
population: Three ChatGPT-generated six-week running plans rated by coaching experts on 22 literature-derived quality criteria
findings: Three plans were generated with increasing input granularity and rated by coaching experts on a 1-5 Likert scale across 22 criteria (Friedman test).
A median rating below 3 was given for 19, 11 and 1 criteria for plans 1, 2 and 3; a median of 3 for 3, 5 and 8; a median above 3 for 0, 6 and 13.
Plan 1 was rated significantly lower than plan 2 on 3 criteria and lower than plan 3 on 15; plan 2 lower than plan 3 on 9 (p < 0.05).
Authors conclude ChatGPT plans were ranked sub-optimally, quality rising with more input, and advise avoiding use without an expert coach's feedback.
limitations: Three plans from one chatbot version; rater count not in abstract; subjective Likert ratings; no outcomes or injuries measured.
implications: Generate sessions with a deterministic rule-based engine seeded by structured inputs; use LLMs only for explanation text.
Collect granular history, availability and goal before generating, since quality rose with input detail.
Turn the idea of an expert quality checklist (progression, recovery weeks, intensity distribution, taper) into automated tests on generated plans.

verification.notes: Crossref: title, J Sports Sci Med, 2024-03-01, first author Düking match. Abstract (PMID 38455449) re-read; added the plan 1 vs 2 result (3 criteria) and median-3 counts.
